members.name: CLUSTER
members.docs:
Peer-to-peer strategy that supports an M-to-N, or cluster-shaped, connection topology.

No restrictions on the amount of incoming and outgoing connections.

members.name: STAR
members.docs:
Peer-to-peer strategy that supports a 1-to-N, or star-shaped, connection topology.

Restricts the discoverer to a single connection, while advertisers have no restrictions on amount of connections.

members.name: POINT_TO_POINT
members.docs:
Peer-to-peer strategy that supports a 1-to-1 connection topology.

Restricts both adverisers and discoverers to a single connection.

members.name: BALANCED
members.docs: Nearby Connections will change the device's Wi-Fi or Bluetooth status only if necessary.

members.name: DISRUPTIVE
members.docs: Nearby Connections will change the device's Wi-Fi or Bluetooth status to enhance throughput.

members.name: NON_DISRUPTIVE
members.docs: Nearby Connections should not change the device's Wi-Fi or Bluetooth status.

members.name: BYTES
members.docs: A Payload consisting of a single byte array.

members.name: FILE
members.docs: A Payload representing a file on the device.

members.name: STREAM
members.docs: A Payload representing a real-time stream of data; e.g. generated data for which the total size is not known ahead of time.

members.name: SUCCESS
members.docs: The remote endpoint has successfully received the full transfer.

members.name: CANCELED
members.docs: Either the local or remote endpoint has canceled the transfer.

members.name: FAILURE
members.docs: The remote endpoint failed to receive the transfer.

members.name: IN_PROGRESS
members.docs: The the transfer is currently in progress with an associated progress value.

members.name: UNKNOWN
members.docs: The manager’s state is unknown.

members.name: RESETTING
members.docs: A state that indicates the connection with the system service was momentarily lost.

members.name: UNSUPPORTED
members.docs: A state that indicates this device doesn’t support the Bluetooth low energy central or client role.

members.name: UNAUTHORIZED
members.docs: A state that indicates the application isn’t authorized to use the Bluetooth low energy role.

members.name: POWERED_OFF
members.docs: A state that indicates Bluetooth is currently powered off.

members.name: POWERED_ON
members.docs: A state that indicates Bluetooth is currently powered on and available to use.

members.name: OK
members.docs: The operation was successful.

members.name: ERROR
members.docs: The operation failed, without any more information.

members.name: ALREADY_ADVERTISING
members.docs: The app is already advertising; call `stopAdvertising()` before trying to advertise again.

members.name: ALREADY_DISCOVERING
members.docs: The app is already discovering the specified application ID; call `stopDiscovery()` before trying to advertise again.

members.name: ALREADY_CONNECTED_TO_ENDPOINT
members.docs:
The app is already connected to the specified endpoint.
Multiple connections to a remote endpoint cannot be maintained simultaneously.

members.name: CONNECTION_REJECTED
members.docs: The remote endpoint rejected the connection request.

members.name: NOT_CONNECTED_TO_ENDPOINT
members.docs: The remote endpoint is not connected; messages cannot be sent to it.

members.name: RADIO_ERROR
members.docs: There was an error trying to use the phone's Bluetooth/WiFi/NFC capabilities.

members.name: ALREADY_HAVE_ACTIVE_STRATEGY
members.docs:
The app already has active operations (advertising, discovering, or connected to other devices) with another `Strategy`.
Stop these operations on the current `Strategy` before trying to advertise or discover with a new `Strategy`.

members.name: OUT_OF_ORDER_API_CALL
members.docs: The app called an API method out of order (i.e. another method is expected to be called first).

members.name: ENDPOINT_UNKNOWN
members.docs: An attempt to interact with a remote endpoint failed because it's unknown to us -- it's either an endpoint that was never discovered, or an endpoint that never connected to us (both of which are indicative of bad input from the client app).

members.name: ENDPOINT_IO_ERROR
members.docs: An attempt to read from/write to a connected remote endpoint failed.

members.name: PAYLOAD_IO_ERROR
members.docs: An attempt to read/write data for a `Payload` of type `FILE` or `STREAM` failed.

members.name: ALREADY_IN_USE
members.docs: This error indicates that Nearby Connections is already in use by some app, and thus is currently unavailable to the caller.

members.name: LOW
members.docs:
The connection quality is poor (5KBps) and is not suitable for sending files.
It's recommended you wait until the connection quality improves.

members.name: MEDIUM
members.docs:
The connection quality is ok (60~200KBps) and is suitable for sending small files.
For large files, it's recommended you wait until the connection quality improves.

members.name: HIGH
members.docs:
The connection quality is good or great (6MBps~60MBps) and files can readily be sent.
The connection quality cannot improve further but may still be impacted by environment or hardware limitations.

typeAliases.name: ServiceID
typeAliases.docs: Used to represent a service identifier.

typeAliases.name: EndpointFoundCallback
typeAliases.docs: Called when a remote endpoint is discovered.

typeAliases.name: EndpointLostCallback
typeAliases.docs: Called when a remote endpoint is no longer discoverable.

typeAliases.name: EndpointInitiatedCallback
typeAliases.docs:
A basic encrypted channel has been created between you and the endpoint.
Both sides are now asked if they wish to accept or reject the connection before any data can be sent over this channel.

typeAliases.name: EndpointConnectedCallback
typeAliases.docs:
Called after both sides have accepted the connection.
Both sides may now send Payloads to each other.

typeAliases.name: EndpointRejectedCallback
typeAliases.docs:
Called when either side rejected the connection.
Payloads can not be exchaged.

typeAliases.name: EndpointDisconnectedCallback
typeAliases.docs:
Called when a remote endpoint is disconnected or has become unreachable.
At this point service (re-)discovery may start again.

typeAliases.name: EndpointBandwidthChangedCallback
typeAliases.docs: Called when a connection is established or if the connection quality improves to a higher connection bandwidth.

typeAliases.name: PayloadReceivedCallback
typeAliases.docs:
Called when a payload is received from a remote endpoint. Depending on the type of the payload,
all of the data may or may not have been received at the time of this call.

typeAliases.name: PayloadTransferUpdateCallback
typeAliases.docs: Called with progress information about an active payload transfer, either incoming or outgoing.
